sections.section_title: Introduction to the Vaikhānasas and their Distinction
sections.content: This section introduces the Vaikhānasas as a small, ancient, and endogamous community of temple-priests in South India (Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu). It establishes their Vedic affiliation with the Taittiriya division of the Kṛṣṇa-Yajurveda. A key point is their distinct identity from other Śrī-vaiṣṇava groups; they do not recognize Rāmānuja or the Āḻvārs in their lineage (guru-paramparā) and do not use Tamil hymns in their worship. The philosophy of the Vaikhānasas is presented as Lakṣmī-Viśiṣṭādvaita, articulated by Śrīnivāsa-makhin, which posits that the path to emancipation is iconic worship (samūrtārcanā) with devotion (bhakti), a practice considered superior to both sacrificial worship (yajana) and the pursuit of knowledge of Brahman (brahma-vidyā).
sections.summary: The Vaikhānasas are an ancient, Vedic-affiliated community of South Indian temple-priests, distinct from Śrī-vaiṣṇavas, who prioritize iconic worship of Viṣṇu as the supreme path to liberation.

sections.section_title: Vaikhānasa Worship: Vedic Roots and Temple Practice
sections.content: This part details the Vaikhānasa mode of worship, emphasizing its exclusive use of Vedic mantras and adherence to Vedic sacraments and fire-rituals. It lists numerous ancient Viṣṇu temples where this tradition is followed. The section highlights the Vaikhānasa belief that their practices, including iconic worship, are not a later innovation but are themselves a form of Vedic ritual, as taught by their founding sage Vikhanas. This view contrasts with other Āgamic traditions like Śaiva and Pāñcarātra, which often see the Āgama as distinct from the Vedic Nigama. Vaikhānasas refer to their scripture as 'bhagavac-cāstra' and see iconic worship as a direct, Vedic-sanctioned practice, supported by texts like the Bhāgavata-purāṇa.
sections.summary: Vaikhānasa worship is strictly Vedic, using only Sanskrit mantras and fire-rituals. They view iconic worship not as a break from Vedic tradition but as an integral and superior part of it, distinct from how other Āgamic schools view their relationship with the Vedas.

sections.section_title: The Transition from Sacrificial Ritual to Temple Worship
sections.content: This section explains the Vaikhānasa rationale for prioritizing iconic worship over fire-rituals. It argues that while various forms of aniconic worship (amūrtārcanā) exist, iconic worship (samūrtārcanā or arcanā) is superior because it is more effective, better suited to the common folk, and directly engages devotion (bhakti). The text outlines a detailed correspondence between the Vedic sacrificial cult and temple worship. The three sacrificial fires (tretāgni: gārhapatya, āhavanīya, dakṣiṇāgni) are mapped onto the three main icons in a temple (bimba-traya: dhruva-bera, kautuka-bera, autsava-bera). Similarly, daily and annual Vedic sacrifices (agni-hotra, Soma-yāga) are transformed into daily and annual temple rituals (nityārcanā, kālotsava). This demonstrates how Vaikhānasas institutionalized temple worship within a Vedic framework.
sections.summary: Vaikhānasas systematically translated the Vedic sacrificial system into the language of temple worship, establishing a direct correspondence between sacrificial fires and temple icons, and between periodic sacrifices and temple festivals, thus framing iconic worship as the evolution of Vedic ritual.

sections.section_title: The Vaikhānasa as a Hermit Tradition (Vānaprastha)
sections.content: This section delves into the ancient origins of the Vaikhānasas, tracing their identity to a specific group of forest-dwelling hermits (vānaprasthas) mentioned in early texts like the Brāhmaṇas, Smṛtis, and Epics. 'Vaikhānasa' is shown to be synonymous with the third stage of life (vānaprastha). The distinguishing feature of these hermits was the tending of a special sacrificial fire called 'śrāmaṇakāgni', following the procedures of the 'śrāmaṇaka' scripture, which is identified as the Vaikhānasa-sūtra. The text describes the austere lifestyle of these hermits, their diet, their relationship with family, and their observance of niyamas and yamas, all while maintaining their Vedic sacrificial duties in a non-materialistic way.
sections.summary: The historical roots of the Vaikhānasas lie in an ancient Vedic hermit tradition of vānaprasthas, distinguished by their unique practice of tending the 'śrāmaṇakāgni' (hermit's fire) according to their own specific scriptures (Vaikhānasa-sūtra).

sections.section_title: The Vaikhānasa Kalpa-sūtras and Vedic Literature
sections.content: The chapter provides a detailed overview of the Vaikhānasa-Kalpa-sūtra's place within the broader corpus of Vedic auxiliary texts (Vedāṅgas). It surveys the Kalpa-sūtras associated with each of the four Vedas, situating the Vaikhānasa text within the Taittirīya faction of the Kṛṣṇa-Yajurveda. The Vaikhānasa-Kalpa-sūtra is described as 'complete' (pari-pūrṇa), as it contains all major sections: Śrauta (public ritual), Gṛhya/Smārta (domestic ritual), and Dharma (law/conduct). It is also known as the 'Vaikhānasa-bhagavac-cāstra'. The text discusses a classification of Kalpa-sūtras into 'earlier' (pūrva) sacrificial texts and 'later' (apara) philosophical and worship-oriented texts, placing the Vaikhānasa-sūtra in the latter category, marking a transition towards Āgamic thought while remaining deeply rooted in the Kalpa-sūtra framework.
sections.summary: The Vaikhānasa-Kalpa-sūtra is a 'complete' Vedic text from the Kṛṣṇa-Yajurveda school, encompassing ritual, domestic, and legal codes. It is considered a 'later' sūtra that uniquely bridges the gap between the older Vedic sacrificial tradition and the newer Āgamic temple worship tradition.

sections.content: This final section focuses on the theological underpinnings of Vaikhānasa worship of Viṣṇu. It argues that Vaikhānasas were responsible for preserving the Vedic character of Viṣṇu into the classical and Āgamic periods. Viṣṇu's Vedic attributes—his three strides, solar associations, and identification with the sacrifice ('yajño vai Viṣṇuḥ')—are central to their theology. The chapter re-interprets a Ṛgvedic hymn (1.155.1) to find scriptural sanction for iconic worship ('arcanā'). It concludes by describing the three main forms of worship recognized in Vaikhānasa texts (e.g., Bhṛgu's Kriyādhikāra): mental worship (mānasi), fire worship (homa-pūjā), and iconic worship (bera-pūjā), with the last being declared the most superior because it directly engages the senses and fosters devotion (bhakti).
sections.summary: Vaikhānasa theology centers on a Vedic Viṣṇu, identified with the sun and the sacrifice itself. They justify iconic worship through Vedic interpretation and classify it as the highest of three forms of worship (mental, fire, iconic) because of its power to evoke devotion.

chapter_summary: Chapter I, 'Historical Perspective', provides a comprehensive overview of the Vaikhānasa community, establishing them as an ancient and distinct group of Vedic temple-priests in South India. The author argues that they are not a subgroup of Śrī-vaiṣṇavism, as they do not recognize key figures like Rāmānuja and the Āḻvārs. Their philosophy and practice are rooted in the Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa-Yajurveda, and their core tenet is the superiority of iconic worship (samūrtārcanā) of Viṣṇu as a direct and evolved form of Vedic sacrifice (yajña). The chapter traces their origins to a vānaprastha (forest hermit) tradition and details how they systematically translated the Vedic sacrificial framework into the rituals and architecture of temple culture, mapping sacrificial fires to temple icons. It examines their primary scripture, the 'complete' Vaikhānasa-Kalpa-sūtra, positioning it as a unique bridge between the older Vedic (Nigama) and newer temple-based (Āgama) traditions. Ultimately, the chapter credits the Vaikhānasas with institutionalizing the worship of a thoroughly Vedic Viṣṇu within a temple context, championing iconic worship as the most effective path for fostering devotion (bhakti).
key_arguments: The Vaikhānasa community is an independent, ancient religious group with a distinct identity, not a sub-sect of Śrī-vaiṣṇavism.

Vaikhānasa philosophy considers iconic worship (samūrtārcanā) with devotion (bhakti) to be the highest form of spiritual practice, superior even to Vedic sacrifice (yajana) and the path of knowledge (brahma-vidyā).
Iconic worship in the Vaikhānasa tradition is not an innovation or a departure from Vedic principles but is itself a Vedic ritual, a direct continuation and sublimation of the sacrificial cult.
The Vaikhānasas played a pivotal role in the historical transition from the age of Vedic sacrifice to the age of temple worship by creating a systematic correspondence between the two.

The Vaikhānasa scriptures (Kalpa-sūtra and the derivative 'bhagavac-cāstra') are unique in that they are both deeply rooted in the Vedic Kalpa-sūtra framework and form the basis of an Āgamic temple tradition.
key_takeaways: Vaikhānasas are Vedic priests who worship Viṣṇu in temples using only Sanskrit mantras.
They are different from Śrī-vaiṣṇavas (who follow Rāmānuja and use Tamil hymns).
They believe temple worship is a higher form of Vedic fire sacrifice.
The three main icons in their temples correspond to the three sacred fires of a Vedic household.
Their tradition originated with ancient forest hermits (vānaprasthas).
Their primary text is the Vaikhānasa-Kalpa-sūtra, a 'complete' Vedic scripture.

historical_figures.name: Rāmānuja
historical_figures.significance: Not recognized in the Vaikhānasa guru-paramparā. He favoured the Pāñcarātra mode of worship, contrasting with the Vaikhānasa system.

historical_figures.name: Āḻvārs
historical_figures.significance: Not recognized or worshipped in the Vaikhānasa tradition; their Tamil hymns are not sung.

historical_figures.name: Śrīnivāsa-makhin
historical_figures.significance: Authored a commentary on the Brahma-sūtras, the Lakṣmī-Viśiṣṭād-vaita-bhāṣya, establishing the distinct Vaikhānasa philosophical position.

historical_figures.name: Nātha-muni
historical_figures.significance: Leader who helped form the Śrī-vaiṣṇava group; the Vaikhānasa community predates him.

historical_figures.name: Yāmuna
historical_figures.significance: Leader of the Śrī-vaiṣṇava group; the Vaikhānasa community predates him.

historical_figures.name: Vikhanas
historical_figures.role: Founding sage of the Vaikhānasa tradition
historical_figures.significance: Believed to have written the Kalpa-sūtra (for householders) and taught the Daivika-sūtra (for iconic worship).

historical_figures.name: Marīci, Atri, Bhrgu, Kāśyapa
historical_figures.role: Four disciples of the sage Vikhanas
historical_figures.significance: They amplified the teachings of Vikhanas, and many Vaikhānasa texts are attributed to them.

historical_figures.name: Baudhāyana
historical_figures.role: Ancient smṛti-kāra and author of a Dharma-sūtra
historical_figures.significance: Acknowledged the Vedic authority of the Vaikhānasa scriptures.

historical_figures.name: Vallabha
historical_figures.significance: His commentary Subodhini suggests that the 'Vaidika' worship mentioned in the Bhāgavata-purāṇa refers to the Vaikhānasa tradition.
historical_figures.dates: 1479–1531 CE (not stated in text, but known)

historical_figures.name: Vīrarāghava
historical_figures.significance: Commented on the Bhāgavata-purāṇa, explaining the two approaches of 'veda' and 'tantra'.

historical_figures.name: Manu
historical_figures.significance: His Manu-smṛti counts the Vaikhānasa-sūtra among great authorities.

historical_figures.name: Gautama
historical_figures.significance: Accepts the authoritative character of the Vaikhānasa-sūtra.

historical_figures.name: Govindasvāmi
historical_figures.significance: Identified Vaikhānasa as a type of vānaprastha.

historical_figures.name: Haradatta
historical_figures.significance: Explained the Śrāmaṇaka method of kindling the sacred fire.

historical_figures.name: Kullūka-bhaṭṭa
historical_figures.significance: Mentioned the Vaikhānasas had their own ideology and doctrine.

historical_figures.name: Kālidāsa
historical_figures.significance: His play 'Śākuntalam' refers to the Vaikhānasa as a life of austerity and vows.
historical_figures.dates: c. 4th-5th century CE (not stated in text)

historical_figures.name: Hārīta
historical_figures.significance: Provided details on the austere life of a Vaikhānasa hermit.

historical_figures.name: Yajñasvāmi
historical_figures.significance: Explained that 'śrāmaṇaka' means the Vaikhānasa-scripture.

historical_figures.name: Bodhāyana
historical_figures.significance: Described the life of a Vaikhānasa hermit.

historical_figures.name: Nṛsimha-vājapeya-yāji
historical_figures.significance: Prepared an elaborate gloss on the Gṛhya and Dharma sections of the Vaikhānasa-sūtra, which provides the framework for the Vaikhānasa-āgama.

historical_figures.name: Vaidyanātha
historical_figures.significance: His Varṇāśramācāra-kāṇḍa classifies Kalpa-sūtras into two groups, 'earlier' and 'later'.

historical_figures.name: J. Gonda
historical_figures.significance: His analysis on the use of Vedic mantras in Vaikhānasa ritual texts is cited.

historical_figures.name: T. Gaṇapati Śāstri
historical_figures.significance: Published the Vaikhānasa text in Devanagari characters in 1913.

historical_figures.name: Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭācārya
historical_figures.significance: Edited a Telugu character edition of Vaikhānasa texts in 1915.

historical_figures.name: W. Caland
historical_figures.significance: Published an edition of Vaikhānasa Gṛhya and Dharma-sūtras in 1925 and 1927.

historical_figures.name: Dr. Eggers
historical_figures.significance: Published the Vaikhānasa-Dharma-sūtras in 1929.

historical_figures.name: R. Pārthasārathi Bhaṭṭācārya
historical_figures.significance: Edited modern editions of Vaikhānasa texts published by TTD and Vaikhānasa-mahāmaṇḍali.

historical_figures.name: R. Śrīnivāsācārya
historical_figures.significance: Edited the Srauta section of the Vaikhānasa-kalpa-sūtra in 1987.

historical_figures.name: Indra
historical_figures.significance: Frequently associated and identified with Viṣṇu. The Vaikhānasa sages were said to be dear to him.

historical_figures.name: Yāska
historical_figures.significance: His Nirukta is cited for the etymology of 'Viṣṇu' and the view of a single divinity appearing in multiple forms.

historical_figures.name: Aurṇavābha
historical_figures.significance: Interpreted Viṣṇu's three strides as the sun's movement at morning, midday, and evening.

historical_figures.name: Śākapūṇi
historical_figures.significance: Interpreted Viṣṇu's three strides as the sun's passage through earth, mid-region, and heaven.

historical_figures.name: Dīrghatama-aucathya
historical_figures.significance: Composer of the Ṛgveda hymn (1.155.1) which Vaikhānasas interpret as justifying iconic worship.

historical_figures.name: Sāyaṇa
historical_figures.significance: His interpretation of 'arcata' as 'acquire well' is cited and rejected by the author in favor of the 'worship' interpretation.

historical_figures.name: Śaunaka
historical_figures.significance: His Ṛgvidhāna is cited to support the interpretation of 'arcata' as worship.

historical_figures.name: Vasiṣṭha
historical_figures.significance: Cited as an ancient authority for the worship of Viṣṇu.

historical_figures.name: Sanaka
historical_figures.significance: Cited as an ancient authority for the worship of Viṣṇu.

historical_events.event: Life of Nātha-muni, early Śrī-vaiṣṇava ācārya.
historical_events.significance: The Vaikhānasa community is established as being an independent entity before the formation of the Śrī-vaiṣṇava group under his leadership.
Further establishes the historical precedence of the Vaikhānasa tradition.

historical_events.event: Flourishing of Śrīnivāsa-makhin, a Vaikhānasa ācārya.
historical_events.significance: He authored a key Vaikhānasa philosophical text, demonstrating a well-developed, independent intellectual tradition concurrent with early Śrī-vaiṣṇavism.

historical_events.event: Life of Rāmānuja, pre-eminent Śrī-vaiṣṇava ācārya.
historical_events.significance: His non-recognition by Vaikhānasas is a central marker of their distinct identity.

historical_events.event: German indologists notice Vaikhānasa Kalpa-sūtra texts.
historical_events.significance: Marks the beginning of modern academic study of Vaikhānasa literature in the West.

historical_events.event: T. Gaṇapati Śāstri publishes Vaikhānasa text in Devanagari.
historical_events.significance: An important step in making the primary texts available to a wider scholarly audience in India.

historical_events.event: W. Caland publishes editions of Vaikhānasa Gṛhya and Dharma-sūtras.
historical_events.significance: Key critical editions that became standard references for Western scholarship on the Vaikhānasas.
Continued the trend of critical European scholarship on Vaikhānasa texts.

geographic_locations.place: Āndhra Pradesh, Karnāṭaka and Tamiḻ Nāḍu
geographic_locations.context: The three states in South India where the Vaikhānasa community is spread.
geographic_locations.significance: Defines the geographical extent of the community.

geographic_locations.place: Kerala or the coastal region of Karnāṭaka
geographic_locations.context: Regions in South India where the Vaikhānasa community is not found.
geographic_locations.significance: Further refines the specific geographic distribution.

geographic_locations.context: A long list of ancient Viṣṇu temples where worship is conducted according to Vaikhānasa prescriptions.
geographic_locations.significance: Demonstrates the historical importance and prevalence of the Vaikhānasa tradition in major South Indian shrines.

geographic_locations.context: Shrines associated with Rāmānuja and the Āḻvārs that continue to have Vaikhānasa priests.
geographic_locations.significance: Highlights the deep-rooted presence of the Vaikhānasa tradition, persisting even in centers of Śrī-vaiṣṇavism.

geographic_locations.context: Mentioned as regions where various factions of Vedic Kalpa-sūtras are followed.
geographic_locations.significance: Provides a broader geographical context for the different Vedic schools in India.

geographic_locations.context: A 1915 edition of Vaikhānasa texts in Telugu characters was published here.

geographic_locations.place: Utrecht, New Delhi, Gottingen, Leipzig, Trivandrum
geographic_locations.context: Locations where key scholarly editions and studies of Vaikhānasa texts were published.
geographic_locations.significance: Shows the global and Indian centers of modern academic research on the Vaikhānasa tradition.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: A community of temple-priests; followers of the sage Vikhanas; also synonymous with vānaprastha.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The main subject of the chapter.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: A major branch of Vaishnavism, particularly associated with Rāmānuja.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Used as a point of contrast to define the Vaikhānasa tradition.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: A division or school of the Kṛṣṇa-Yajurveda.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The specific Vedic affiliation of the Vaikhānasa community.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Lineage of spiritual preceptors.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The Vaikhānasas do not include Rāmānuja or the Āḻvārs in theirs.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Iconic worship; worship of a form.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The central and superior mode of worship in the Vaikhānasa system.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Devotion.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: An essential component of samūrtārcanā.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Worship, meditation.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Equated with 'yajana' and considered a different, less superior approach than samūrtārcanā by Vaikhānasas.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Worship as a sacrifice.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The core concept of Vedic ritual, which Vaikhānasas see as fulfilled and surpassed by iconic worship.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Wisdom concerning Brahman; knowledge of the Absolute.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Iconic worship is held to be more effective than even this.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: A major Vaiṣṇava Āgamic tradition, favoured by Rāmānuja.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Contrasted with the Vaikhānasa tradition, particularly in its relationship to the Vedas.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: A type of Vedic ancillary text (Vedāṅga) dealing with rituals.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The foundational scripture for the Vaikhānasa tradition.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: A body of sectarian scriptures, especially concerning temple worship.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Vaikhānasas represent a unique Āgama tradition that is fully integrated with the Vedic Kalpa-sūtra framework.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: The Vedas.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The term used to distinguish the Vedic approach from the Āgamic one in other traditions.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Scripture of the Lord.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The Vaikhānasa term for their own scriptures, emphasizing their divine origin.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Aniconic worship; worship of the formless.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Refers primarily to fire-rituals, contrasted with samūrtārcanā.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Worship, particularly of an icon.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Synonymous with samūrtārcanā, considered the highest form of worship.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Pertaining to public Vedic sacrifices prescribed in the Śrutis.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: A major section of the Kalpa-sūtras, de-emphasized by Vaikhānasas due to its association with worldly desires.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Pertaining to domestic Vedic rituals.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: A major section of the Kalpa-sūtras, stressed by Vaikhānasas.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: The main, immovable icon in the sanctum.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Corresponds to the gārhapatya sacrificial fire.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: The movable icon used for daily worship (nityārcanā).
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Corresponds to the āhavanīya sacrificial fire.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: The processional icon used for festivals.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Corresponds to the dakṣiṇāgni sacrificial fire.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Forest-dweller; the third of the four stages of life (āśramas).
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The original lifestyle of the Vaikhānasa sages.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: The hermit's fire.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The characteristic sacrificial fire tended by Vaikhānasa hermits.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Sacramental rite; life-cycle ritual.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: The Vaikhānasa Gṛhya-sūtras detail eighteen of these.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Offering to Viṣṇu.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: A sacrament unique to the Vaikhānasas.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: The sacrifice is indeed Viṣṇu.
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: A key Vedic equation underpinning the Vaikhānasa integration of sacrifice and Viṣṇu worship.

sanskrit_hindi_terms.translation: Worship of the icon (bera).
sanskrit_hindi_terms.context: Another term for iconic worship, considered the best of three types.

quotations.quote:
लक्ष्मीविशिष्टः नारायणः अद्वैतं यत्र ।
मते तत् लक्ष्मीविशिष्टाद्वैतम
quotations.context: To define the Vaikhānasa philosophical position of Lakṣmī-Viśiṣṭādvaita.

quotations.quote:
'तस्मादग्नौ नित्यहोमान्ते विष्णुर्नित्यार्चा गृहे देवायतने
भक्त्या भगवन्तं नारायणमर्चयेत् ।
quotations.context: To show that iconic worship of Viṣṇu is a Vedic ritual that follows the daily fire oblation.

quotations.quote:
यज्वभिर्यज्ञपुरुषो वासुदेवश्च सात्वतैः ।
वेदान्तवेदिभिर्विष्णुः प्रोच्यते यो नतोऽस्मि तम्॥
quotations.context: To distinguish the Vaikhānasa worship of 'Viṣṇu' from the worship of 'yajña-puruṣa' by ritualists and 'Vāsudeva' by Pāñcarātras.

quotations.quote:
साकारं च निराकारं भवत्याराधनं द्विधा ।
प्रतिमाराधनं श्रेष्टं साकारमभिधीयते ।।
... 
विशेषभक्तिहेतुत्वात् प्रतिमाराधनं वरम्।
quotations.context: To argue for the superiority of iconic (sākāram) worship over aniconic (nirākāram) worship.

quotations.quote:
तदर्चनं द्विधा प्रोक्तमूर्तं च समूर्तम्।
अग्नौ हुतममूर्त स्यात् समूर्त बेरपूजनम् ।।
quotations.source: Not specified, likely a Vaikhānasa text
quotations.context: To define the two types of worship: aniconic (amūrtam) as fire oblation and iconic (samūrtam) as icon worship.

quotations.quote:
अमूर्तं यजमानस्य ह्यभावे च विनश्यति ।
अच्छिन्नं शाश्वतं नित्यं प्रतिमाराधनं परम्।।
quotations.context: To contrast the temporary benefits of sacrificial rituals with the eternal benefits of iconic worship.

quotations.quote:
स्थापितां प्रतिमां विष्णोः सम्यकसंपूज्य मानवः ।
... 
कल्पद्रुमादिव हरेर्यदिष्टं तदवाप्यते ॥
quotations.context: To state that iconic worship can fulfill all desires and bestow the benefits of all sacrifices.

quotations.quote:
तपसां श्रमणमेतन्मूलं तस्मादेतद्विधानमेतदग्निं च ।
श्रामणकमित्याह भगवान् ।
quotations.context: To suggest that the sage Vikhanas himself coined the term 'śrāmaṇaka' for the hermit's way of life and fire-ritual.

quotations.quote: वैखानसा वा ऋषयः इन्द्रस्य प्रिया आसन्
quotations.context: To establish the ancient Vedic connection of Vaikhānasa sages as being dear to Indra (Viṣṇu).

quotations.quote:
पुष्यमूलफलैर्वापि कवलैर्वर्तयेत् सदा ।
कालपक्वैः स्वयंशीर्णैर्वैखानसमते स्थितः ॥
quotations.context: To describe the prescribed austere diet of a Vaikhānasa hermit.

quotations.quote:
तेषु वैखानसा नाम वानप्रस्थाः शुभेक्षणे ।
तीव्रेण तपसा युक्ता दीप्तिमन्तः सुतेजसाः।
quotations.context: To describe Vaikhānasa hermits as engaged in extreme penance.

quotations.quote: श्रामणकेनाग्निमाधाय आहिताग्निः वृक्षमूलिकः ।
quotations.context: To prescribe the installation of the sacrificial fire according to the 'śrāmaṇaka' procedure for a Vaikhānasa.

quotations.quote: श्रामणकं नाम वैखानसं शास्त्रम् । तदुक्तेन विधिना ।
quotations.context: To explicitly define 'śrāmaṇaka' as the Vaikhānasa scripture.

quotations.quote:
वानप्रस्थो वैखानसशास्त्रसमुदाचारो वने मूलफलशी
...
न फलकृष्टमधितिष्ठेत् ग्रामं वा प्रविशेत्।
quotations.context: A detailed description of the Vaikhānasa hermit's code of conduct.

quotations.quote:
बोधायनीयापस्तंम्बीयं सत्याषाढं गागयसमागस्त्य
शाकल्यमाश्वलायनं शांभवीयं कात्यायनमिति नवानि
पूर्वसूत्राणि ।
वैखानसीयं शौनकीयं भारद्वाजं याज्ञवल्क्यं जैमिनीयं
वाधूलं माध्यन्दिनं कौण्डिण्यं कौषीतकीयमिति
नवान्यपरसूत्राणि ।
quotations.context: To list the nine 'earlier' and nine 'later' Kalpa-sūtra manuals.

quotations.quote: मन्थमात्मानं विष्णुं जन्यमग्नि च ध्यायन्। (1, 10,5)
quotations.context: Prescribing contemplation on Viṣṇu as the fire generated from the friction of the worshipper's own self.

quotations.quote: अथाग्नौ नित्यहोमान्ते विष्णोर्नित्यार्चा सर्वदेर्वार्चा भवति। (९५)
quotations.context: Stating that after the daily fire oblation, worshipping Viṣṇu constitutes worship of all gods.

quotations.quote:
प्रवप्रः पान्तमन्धसो धियायते
महे शूराय विष्णवे चार्चते ।
या सानुनि पर्वतानामदभ्या
महस्तस्थतुरर्वतेव साधुना ।।
quotations.context: Interpreted by Vaikhānasa commentators as a Vedic justification for the iconic worship ('arcate') of Viṣṇu.

quotations.quote:
तं यज्ञपुरुषं ध्यायन् पुरुषसूक्तेन संस्तूय प्रणामं कुर्यात्।
यज्ञेषु विहीनं तत् सम्पूर्ण भवतीति श्रुतिः ।
quotations.context: Stating that devotion to Viṣṇu (the Yajña-puruṣa) compensates for any deficiencies in sacrifices.

quotations.quote:
सर्वे वैदिकाचारास्तपोयज्ञाश्च विष्णुपूजाविधेर्भेदाः ।
इति वैखानससूत्रम्।
quotations.context: A statement claiming that all Vedic rites, austerities, and sacrifices are simply different forms of Viṣṇu worship.

quotations.quote:
मानसी होमपूजेति बेरपूजेति सा त्रिधाा।
...
तस्मात्त्रयाणमेतेषां बेरपूजा विशिष्यते ॥
quotations.context: A long passage detailing the three types of worship (mental, fire, and iconic) and concluding that iconic worship (bera-pūjā) is superior.

controversial_points: The author's classification of Kalpa-sūtras into 'pūrva' (earlier/general) and 'apara' (later/non-general) groups is noted by the author himself as having a basis that is 'not very clear'.

The interpretation of the Ṛgvedic word 'arcata' (in RV 1.155.1) as a direct injunction for iconic worship is a specific Vaikhānasa sectarian view, which is contested by other traditional commentators like Sāyaṇa.

The claim that the Vaikhānasa tradition is purely Vedic (Nigama) and not Āgama, while simultaneously being presented as the forerunner of Āgamic temple worship, represents a complex and potentially debatable positioning of the tradition's identity.
alternative_viewpoints: Śrī-vaiṣṇava viewpoint: Views itself as the primary Vaiṣṇava tradition in the South, incorporating Āḻvār hymns and following the Pāñcarātra Āgama, in contrast to the Vaikhānasa's exclusive Vedic focus.
Śaiva and Pāñcarātra viewpoint: These traditions are said to recognize that the 'Āgama' approach was at variance with the Vedic ('Nigama'), a view the Vaikhānasas reject for their own system.

Sāyaṇa's interpretation: The Vedic commentator Sāyaṇa interprets the word 'arcata' in Ṛgveda 1.155.1 as 'acquire well' ('prakarṣeṇa sampādayatha'), which the author rejects as 'altogether unjustified' in favor of the Vaikhānasa interpretation of 'worship' ('pūjayata').
